entryPoint: Dept::isActive() in include/class.dept.php (lines 179-181). Zero-argument instance method on the Dept ORM model (extends VerySimpleModel), called as $dept->isActive() on an already-loaded Dept object.
coreLogic: Dept::isActive() returns !!($this->flags & self::FLAG_ACTIVE) where FLAG_ACTIVE = 0x0004 (a class const shared with FLAG_ASSIGN_MEMBERS_ONLY=0x0001, FLAG_DISABLE_AUTO_CLAIM=0x0002, FLAG_ARCHIVED=0x0008, FLAG_ASSIGN_PRIMARY_ONLY=0x0010, FLAG_DISABLE_REOPEN_AUTO_ASSIGN=0x0020). This is a single-expression, pure bitwise-AND test against the already-loaded 'flags' property (mapped to the ost_department.flags DB column via VerySimpleModel). There is no sub-delegation below isActive() itself — it is a leaf method, the same shape as the sibling methods getStatus() (lines 166-173, tests FLAG_ACTIVE then FLAG_ARCHIVED to pick a label) and allowsReopen() (lines 175-177, tests FLAG_ARCHIVED). Those siblings are separate facade surfaces reading the same flags property and are out of scope for this ticket's extraction.

inputShape: No parameters. Called on an already-instantiated/loaded Dept model object (via Dept::lookup(), Dept::getParent(), Topic::getDept(), or Staff's 'dept' ORM join) whose 'flags' integer property (ORM-mapped from ost_department.flags) reflects the department's current bit flags: FLAG_ASSIGN_MEMBERS_ONLY=0x0001, FLAG_DISABLE_AUTO_CLAIM=0x0002, FLAG_ACTIVE=0x0004, FLAG_ARCHIVED=0x0008, FLAG_ASSIGN_PRIMARY_ONLY=0x0010, FLAG_DISABLE_REOPEN_AUTO_ASSIGN=0x0020 (flags may have any combination of other bits set concurrently).
outputShape: Returns a native PHP boolean: true if the FLAG_ACTIVE bit (0x0004) is set in $this->flags, false otherwise. Callers use both the direct boolean and its negation (!$dept->isActive()) in conditionals; several callers (e.g. include/class.ticket.php:4260) branch on the negation to trigger a fallback assignment rather than just a validation error. No mutation of the Dept object occurs inside isActive() itself.
sideEffects: None inside isActive() itself — it performs no database reads/writes of its own; it only inspects the 'flags' property already populated on the in-memory Dept object by a prior ORM fetch/lookup (e.g. Dept::lookup(), Dept::getParent(), or a joined 'dept' relation).
No global state ($cfg, $ost, session, etc.) is read or written by isActive() itself.
No lazy-loading is triggered by isActive() itself (unlike Dept::getFullPath() or other Dept accessors that may traverse parent chains).
No caching, file I/O, or logging occurs inside isActive().
No object mutation: $this->flags is only read, never modified, by isActive().

Indirect/caller-side side effect (outside isActive(), but dependent on its return value): include/class.ticket.php:4259-4261 reassigns the local $deptId variable to $cfg->getDefaultDeptId() when isActive() returns false, which reads global $cfg and affects which department a new ticket is created under. This caller-side branching logic must continue to receive the identical boolean from the (patched) facade call.
constraints: Must return true if and only if ($flags & FLAG_ACTIVE) is nonzero; the FLAG_ARCHIVED (0x0008), FLAG_ASSIGN_MEMBERS_ONLY (0x0001), FLAG_DISABLE_AUTO_CLAIM (0x0002), FLAG_ASSIGN_PRIMARY_ONLY (0x0010), and FLAG_DISABLE_REOPEN_AUTO_ASSIGN (0x0020) bits, or any other bits present in flags, must NOT affect the result — only the FLAG_ACTIVE bit matters, even when multiple flags are set simultaneously (e.g. active+archived both set, or active plus assignment/auto-claim flags).

Return type must remain a genuine PHP boolean (current code uses double-negation !!) so strict boolean contexts and negations (!$dept->isActive()) in the 11 live consumer call sites keep working identically.

Method signature must remain unchanged: Dept::isActive() takes no arguments and is called the same way, $dept->isActive(), by every live consumer, including the self-referential call at include/class.dept.php:802 where one Dept instance calls isActive() on a different (parent) Dept instance.

The extracted service must not perform any DB query or reload of the Dept — it must operate solely on the flags value already available on the object/value passed to it, preserving the current zero-side-effect behavior.

The extracted service must NOT be called from, and must NOT call back into, Dept::isActive() (anti-recursion) — the facade method keeps its call site and delegates outward to the new service instead of containing the bitwise logic inline.

The FLAG_ACTIVE constant value (0x0004) must be preserved exactly as the bit tested for Dept; do not confuse it with Topic's FLAG_ACTIVE (0x0002, MOD-31) or SLA's FLAG_ACTIVE (0x0001) which are separate classes with independently-numbered flag constants also named FLAG_ACTIVE.

Dept::getStatus() (lines 166-173) and Dept::allowsReopen() (lines 175-177) read the same $this->flags property with their own inline bitwise tests (FLAG_ACTIVE and FLAG_ARCHIVED) but are separate facade methods not covered by this ticket's isActive() extraction — do not refactor them or route them through the new service.
harnessInputShape: JSON object with a single field: 'flags' (integer) - the raw department flags bitmask to test, matching ost_department.flags semantics (FLAG_ASSIGN_MEMBERS_ONLY=1, FLAG_DISABLE_AUTO_CLAIM=2, FLAG_ACTIVE=4, FLAG_ARCHIVED=8, FLAG_ASSIGN_PRIMARY_ONLY=16, FLAG_DISABLE_REOPEN_AUTO_ASSIGN=32, combinable via bitwise OR). The harness constructs/populates a Dept instance with this flags value (without hitting the DB) and outputs the boolean result of calling isActive() on it, so it can exercise: active only (flags=4), inactive/disabled (flags=0), archived-only (flags=8, FLAG_ACTIVE not set), and active-plus-other-flags (e.g. flags=5 for active+assign-members-only, or flags=12 for active+archived both set) to prove only the FLAG_ACTIVE bit drives the result.
